facts_of_case: Mother filed petition under Section 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act read with Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act for custody of minor. Family Court allowed petition. Father appealed.

legal_principles.principle: The controlling consideration governing the custody of children is the welfare of the children and not the right of the parents.
legal_principles.held: The apex court held that the controlling consideration governing the custody of the children is the welfare of the children and not the right of the parents.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act — Section 6

legal_principles.principle: A minor can always retain the place of residence of his/her mother.
legal_principles.held: But a minor can always retain the place of residence of his/her mother.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act — Section 6

legal_principles.principle: The jurisdiction of the courts to entertain application with respect to the guardianship of the person of the minor is governed by Section 9 of the Guardian and Wards Act.
legal_principles.held: Section 9 of the Guardian and Wards Act deals with jurisdiction of the courts to entertain application with respect to the guardianship of the person of the minor.

legal_principles.principle: The facts and circumstances of each case must be looked into to ascertain whether a person can be said to ordinarily reside at a given place.
legal_principles.held: Learned single Judge of this court in Chandy's case, supra held that the facts and circumstances of each case must be looked into to ascertain whether a person can be said to ordinarily reside at a given place.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act — Section 6

legal_principles.principle: The mere fact that the minor was residing at Bahrain does not mean that a petition at the instance of the mother under Section 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act read with Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act be not entertained by the Family Court.
legal_principles.held: The mere fact that the minor was residing at Bahrain does not mean that a petition at the instance of the mother under Section 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act read with Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act be not entertained by the Family Court.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act — Section 6

outcome.final_order: Family Court's order upholding mother's petition for custody of minor is maintained.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for custody of minor
advising on jurisdiction in family disputes
preparing an appeal against a Family Court order
